 Service & Solidarity Spotlight: IAM Union Members at Long Beach City Ratify Strong Contract, with 8.4% Wage Increases 
 Kenneth Quinnell 
 November 16, 2026 
 Working people across the United States regularly step up to help out our friends, neighbors and communities during these trying times. In our Service & Solidarity Spotlight series, we’ll showcase one of these stories every day. Here’s today’s story. 
 IAM Union Local 1930 members ratified a strong tentative agreement with the city of Long Beach, California, that includes 8.4% general wage increases over three years. The deal awaits City Council approval later this month. 
 Other benefits include targeted equity pay adjustments, signing bonuses, expanded skill pay, increased compensatory time and limits on using artificial intelligence in discipline. 
 “The 2026 Negotiation Team came together from every sector of the city, united by one common goal: to secure the best possible contract for our Local 1930 members,” said Local 1930 President Eligio Garcia. “It was a hard-fought battle, but through teamwork, determination, and solidarity, they stood together and came back with stronger protections for our members. I am incredibly proud of this team, their dedication, and everything they accomplished. They showed what we can achieve when we stand united and fight for one another. Solidarity makes us stronger!”
